blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Shared Authority**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Supervisory Intervention, § Shared Authority
blocks.md: When a pallet blocks an aisle and the warehouse mobile manipulator requests a remote assistant to take over, the transfer introduces a delay that no test on the chassis can bound, because it belongs to a person. Part III left the running machine with a stopping budget whose every term belongs to the hardware, each with a declared bound and a loaded test that could refute it, even where the test has not yet run, as for the dispatch-to-admission interval DispatchAdmissionInterval that a later section allocated but did not measure.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Authority record matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: The authority record binds a sealed static authority manifest to a per-tick evidence tuple of time, authority state, measured state, proposed and admitted commands, so every handover is reconstructable and attributable.

questions.q: The section **Shared Authority** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Protective stops never wait for verification while motion commands, which inject energy, must be authenticated, attributable, and fresh, and the verifier's availability must itself be protected.
A remote assistant is admitted only if reaction budget, handshake latency, manual lease, and blend window fit the remaining clearance, and remote assistance is never a safety layer.

The authority record binds a sealed static authority manifest to a per-tick evidence tuple of time, authority state, measured state, proposed and admitted commands, so every handover is reconstructable and attributable.
Takeover latency (sensory, cognitive, motor, console) is long-tailed and must be budgeted at a design percentile as a delay before braking, which sets the speed a supervised machine may run.
questions.hint: Re-read the excerpt and the section map: which idea is this section building toward?
questions.explanation: This section develops **Authority record**: The authority record binds a sealed static authority manifest to a per-tick evidence tuple of time, authority state, measured state, proposed and admitted commands, so every handover is reconstructable and attributable.
